([[Vaughan, Ontario]]) * [[Montverde Academy]]
([[Montverde, Florida]]) | college = * [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] (2018–2020) * [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] (2020–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 31 | draft_team = [[Indiana Pacers]] | career_start = 2022 | years1 = {{nbay|2022|start}}–present | team1 = [[Indiana Pacers]] | highlights = * First-team All-[[West Coast Conference|WCC]] (2022) * Second-team All-WCC (2021) * WCC Sixth Man of the Year (2021) * [[West Coast Conference men's basketball tournament|WCC tournament]] MOP ([[2022 West Coast Conference men's basketball tournament|2022]]) * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team (2019) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport|Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|CAN}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|FIBA Americas U18 Championship]]}} {{MedalSilver|[[2018 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship|2018 Canada]]|[[Canada men's national under-18 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Andrew William Nembhard''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|n|ɛ|m|h|ɑːr|d}} {{respell|NEM|hard}};{{cite press release |author= |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 17, 2024}} born January 16, 2000) is a Canadian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Indiana Pacers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]] and [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. He was selected by the Pacers with the 31st overall pick in the second round of the [[2022 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |date=June 24, 2022 |title=Pacers select Canadian Andrew Nembhard 31st overall in the 2022 NBA Draft |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/pacers-select-canadian-andrew-nembhard-31st-overall-in-the-2022-nba-draft/ |access-date=October 18, 2025 |website=Sportsnet.ca}} ==College career== [[File:Andrew Nembhard (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Nembhard with [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] in 2020]] Nembhard was recruited to the [[University of Florida]] from [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]]. In his freshman season with the Gators, he started every game and tallied the fourth-highest freshman assist total in school history. After averaging 8.0 points, 2.9 rebounds and 5.4 assists, and finishing fifth in the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) in assist-turnover ratio, Nembhard was named to the conference all-Freshman team.{{cite news |last1= Parler |first1= Denver |title=Nembhard Earns SEC All-Freshman Honors |url=https://floridagators.com/news/2019/3/12/mens-basketball-nembhard-earns-sec-all-freshman-honors.aspx?path=basketball-men |access-date=September 15, 2019 |work=[[Florida Gators]] |date=March 12, 2019}} Just a few days later, Nembhard hit a [[buzzer-beater]] to upset [[LSU Tigers basketball|Louisiana State University]] (LSU) in the [[2019 SEC men's basketball tournament|2019 SEC tournament]].{{cite magazine |last1= Caron |first1= Emily |title=Watch: Florida's Andrew Nemhbard Sinks Last-Second Shot to Upset LSU in SEC Tournament |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2019/03/15/florida-andrew-nembhard-game-winning-shot-lsu-sec-tournament |access-date=September 15, 2019 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=March 15, 2019}} Nembhard declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]], but ultimately chose to return to the Gators for his sophomore season.{{cite news |last1= Thompson |first1= Edgar |title=UF freshman Andrew Nembhard declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/florida-gators/os-sp-gators-basketball-news-20190413-story.html |access-date=September 15, 2019 |work=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |date=April 12, 2019}}{{cite news |title=Canadian guard Nembhard returning to Florida for sophomore season |url=https://www.tsn.ca/canadian-guard-nembhard-returning-to-florida-for-sophomore-season-1.1313576 |access-date=September 15, 2019 |work=[[The Sports Network]] |date=May 29, 2019}} As a sophomore, Nembhard averaged 11.2 points, 5.6 assists, and 3.0 rebounds per game and led the SEC with a 2.2 assist-to-turnover ratio.{{cite news |last1=Collings |first1=Buddy |title=Orlando area college basketball All Stars for 2019-20 |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/boys-basketball/os-sp-hs-college-basketball-best-20200401-ua7uhgocpnhzpow3j52az7y2su-story.html |access-date=April 4, 2020 |work=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |date=April 3, 2020}} Following the season he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] but hired an NCAA-certified agent, allowing him the option to return to Florida.{{cite news |title=Florida guards Andrew Nembhard and Tre Mann declare for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29101274/florida-guard-andrew-nembhard-declares-nba-draft-again |access-date=April 27, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=April 26, 2020}}{{cite news |title=Canadian guard Andrew Nembhard declares for NBA draft again |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/andrew-nembhard-declares-nba-draft-again-canada-1.5545705 |access-date=28 April 2020 |agency=CBC |date=26 April 2020}} On May 30, 2020, Nembhard withdrew from the draft and entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Sources: Andrew Nembhard to exit NBA draft, transfer from Florida |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29245276/sources-andrew-nembhard-exit-nba-draft-transfer-florida |access-date=May 30, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=May 30, 2020}} On June 23, 2020, Nembhard announced that he would transfer to [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]]. He chose the Bulldogs over offers from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]] and [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]].{{cite web |last1=Conway |first1=Tyler |title=Florida Transfer Andrew Nembhard Commits to Gonzaga over Duke, More |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2897343-florida-transfer-andrew-nembhard-commits-to-gonzaga-over-duke-more |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=June 23, 2020 |date=June 23, 2020}} He was granted a waiver for immediate eligibility on November 24.{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Transfer Andrew Nembhard eligible to play for Gonzaga men's basketball |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30382342/transfer-andrew-nembhard-eligible-play-gonzaga-bulldogs |access-date=November 25, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=November 24, 2020}} In his [[2020–21 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|first Gonzaga season]], he primarily came off the bench (though he played more minutes per game than two Bulldogs starters), averaging 9.2 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 4.4 assists per game{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/gonzaga/2021.html |title=2020-21 Gonzaga Bulldogs Roster and Stats |website=Sports Reference CBB |accessdate=March 2, 2021}} for a team that entered its conference tournament unbeaten. Nembhard was named the [[West Coast Conference]]'s inaugural Sixth Man of the Year, and was also named to the all-conference second team.{{cite press release|url=https://wccsports.com/news/2021/3/2/wcc-unveils-2020-21-mens-basketball-all-conference-honors.aspx |title=WCC Unveils 2020-21 Men's Basketball All-Conference Honors |publisher=West Coast Conference |date=March 2, 2021 |accessdate=March 2, 2021}} He averaged 11.8 points, 5.8 assists, 3.4 rebounds and 1.6 steals per game as a senior. Nembhard was named to the First Team All-WCC.{{cite press release|url=https://wccsports.com/news/2022/3/2/mens-basketball-timme-tabbed-wcc-player-of-the-year.aspx|title=Timme Tabbed WCC Player Of The Year|publisher=[[West Coast Conference]] |date=March 2, 2022 |accessdate=March 2, 2022}} On April 21, 2022, Nembhard declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{Cite web |date=2022-04-21 |title=Zags' guard Nembhard to declare for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33778131/gonzaga-bulldogs-senior-andrew-nembhard-declare-2022-nba-draft |access-date=2022-04-21 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} ==Professional career== ===Indiana Pacers (2022–present)=== Nembhard was selected with the 31st overall pick by the [[Indiana Pacers]]. Nembhard joined the Pacers' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] roster.{{Cite web |title=Indiana Pacers 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612754/pacers |access-date=2022-07-23 |website=www.nba.com}} In his Summer League debut, Nembhard scored five points, five rebounds, and five assists in a 96–84 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{Cite web |title=Charlotte Hornets vs Indiana Pacers Jul 8, 2022 Box Scores {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/game/cha-vs-ind-1522200005/box-score#box-score |access-date=2022-07-23 |website=www.nba.com}} On July 22, 2022, Nembhard signed a four–year, $8.6M rookie contract with the Pacers, the largest rookie contract ever given to a second-rounder.{{Cite web |title=Pacers Sign Nembhard |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-nembhard |access-date=2022-07-23 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}{{cite web | last=Boyd | first=James | title=Pacers sign rookie Andrew Nembhard to record deal for 2nd round pick | website=IndyStar | date=2022-07-21 | url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2022/07/21/indiana-pacers-sign-rookie-andrew-nembhard-to-record-deal-for-2nd-round-nba-draft-pick/65378848007/ | access-date=2025-12-08}} On November 28, Nembhard scored a buzzer-beating, game-winning three-pointer in a 116–115 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/pacers-news-nba-twitter-erupts-after-indiana-rookie-sends-lebron-james-lakers-home-crying-with-a-game-winning-triple|title=NBA Twitter erupts after Pacers rookie sends LeBron James, Lakers home crying with a game-winning triple|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=November 28, 2022|access-date=November 28, 2022}} On December 5, with [[Tyrese Haliburton]] injured, Nembhard scored a career-high 31 points, 13 assists, 8 rebounds, and 5 three-pointers in a win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/pacers-rookie-andrew-nembhard-upstages-stephen-curry-with-a-performance-he-wont-ever-forget/|title=Pacers rookie Andrew Nembhard upstages Stephen Curry with a performance he'll never forget|website=CBS NBA|last=Botkin|first=Brad|date=December 6, 2022|access-date=December 6, 2022}} On January 31, 2023, Nembhard was named a [[NBA Rising Stars Challenge|2023 NBA Rising Star]] alongside standout rookie teammate [[Bennedict Mathurin]].{{cite web |title=Pacers' Bennedict Mathurin, Andrew Nembhard named NBA Rising Stars for All-Star Weekend |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2023/01/31/pacers-bennedict-mathurin-andrew-nembhard-named-nba-rising-stars/69858891007/ |website=IndyStar.com |access-date=January 31, 2023 |date=January 31, 2023}} Nembhard recorded back–to–back 20–point games with 24 points on March 16 against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], and 22 points on 9–14 shooting on March 18 against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web |title=Andrew Nembhard (24 Points) Highlights Vs. Milwaukee Bucks |url=https://www.nba.com/watch/video/andrew-nembhard-24-points-highlights-vs-milwaukee-bucks |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 16, 2023 |date=March 16, 2023}}{{cite web |title=Andrew Nembhard (22 Points) Highlights Vs. Philadelphia 76ers |url=https://www.nba.com/watch/video/andrew-nembhard-22-points-highlights-vs-philadelphia-76ers |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 18, 2023 |date=March 18, 2023}} On March 22, in a win against the [[Toronto Raptors]], Nembhard recorded another double–double with 25 points and 10 assists on 11–17 shooting.{{cite web |title=Andrew Nembhard Posts 25 Points & 10 Assists Vs. Toronto Raptors |url=https://www.nba.com/watch/video/andrew-nembhard-posts-25-points-10-assists-vs-toronto-raptors |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 22, 2023 |date=March 22, 2023}} On March 28, as a starter against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], Nembhard recorded a double–double with 15 points and a career–high 15 assists.{{cite web |title=Andrew Nembhard with 15 Assists vs. Milwaukee Bucks |url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/videos/andrew-nembhard-with-15-assists-vs-milwaukee-bucks |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 28, 2023 |date=March 28, 2023}} On May 10, 2024, in a second-round game of the playoffs against the [[New York Knicks]], Nembhard hit a game winning three–pointer with 16 seconds on the clock to help the Pacers extend their series lead to 2–1. The three was the longest of his career up to that point. On July 26, 2024, Nembhard signed a three-year, $59 million extension that would keep him under contract through 2028.{{cite web |date=July 24, 2024 |title=Andrew Nembhard agrees to 3-year, $59M extension with Pacers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40630193/andrew-nembhard-agrees-3-year-59m-extension-pacers |access-date=April 17, 2026 |publisher=espn.com}} ==National team career== Nembhard represented Canada in [[FIBA]] competition at the U-16, U-17 and U-18 levels.{{cite news |last1= McLamb |first1= Michael |title=Andrew Nembhard: Canada's latest great hope |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/andrew-nembhard-canada-fiba-americas |access-date=September 15, 2019 |work=[[USA Today]] |date=June 14, 2018}} In 2019, he made the senior national team for the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA World Cup]].{{cite news |last1= Smith |first1= Doug |title=Aurora teen Andrew Nembhard just might be ready to take on the basketball world |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/basketball/2019/08/09/aurora-teen-andrew-nembhard-just-might-be-ready-to-take-on-the-basketball-world.html |access-date=September 15, 2019 |work=[[Toronto Star]] |date=August 9, 2019}} He was named to Canada's roster for the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Summer Olympics in Paris]].{{cite web| title = Gilgeous-Alexander, Murray to lead NBA-experienced Canadian Olympic team in Paris| publisher = CBC / The Canadian Press | url = https://www.cbc.ca/sports/olympics/summer/basketball/canada-olympic-mens-basketball-roster-paris-1.7259301 | access-date = July 10, 2014}} ==Personal life== Nembhard is of Jamaican descent through his father, Claude. He has one younger brother, [[Ryan Nembhard|Ryan]], who also played basketball at Gonzaga and is currently playing for the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web | last=Lawson | first=Theo | title=Ontario's Very Own: Longtime friends and teammates Andrew Nembhard and Marcus Carr will be rival point guards when No. 1 Gonzaga hosts No. 5 Texas | website=Spokesman.com | date=2021-11-12 |
